keyVerseText: And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
rootMeaning: The name יִשְׁבָּק (Yishbâq) derives from an unused root related to שְׁבַק, which carries the sense of 'he will leave' or 'he releases.' This etymology suggests a meaning tied to separation or setting free, adding a deeper nuance beyond the mere identification as a proper name. The literal sense of release or departure enriches the understanding of this name as more than a label; it conveys an active concept of letting go or sending forth.
usageInScripture: The word יִשְׁבָּק appears only twice in Scripture, consistently translated as 'and Ishbak,' referring to a specific individual. Both occurrences identify Ishbak as a son of Abraham by Keturah, emphasizing his role as a progenitor of an Arabian tribe. The limited but consistent usage underscores the name's function primarily as a genealogical marker within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יִשְׁבָּק as meaning 'he releases' invites reflection on God's providential role in the expansion and fulfillment of His promises through Abraham's descendants. Ishbak, as a son of Abraham, represents part of God's faithful covenant extending beyond Isaac, demonstrating the breadth of God's blessing to many nations. This reminds believers that God's purposes often involve sending forth His people into new contexts, trusting His sovereign plan. The name's meaning also points to the spiritual truth of release and freedom found in Christ, who liberates His people from bondage and commissions them into the world.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 25:2 lists Ishbak among the sons born to Abraham by Keturah: 'And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.' The inclusion of Ishbak here highlights his place in Abraham's lineage and God's unfolding covenant history. The name's meaning, connected to release or sending forth, enriches this verse by suggesting that Ishbak's birth was part of God’s purposeful expansion of Abraham’s family, destined to impact surrounding nations.
